The field is read on the backend by `UndoQueueEntryTransitionRequest` (the DTO's `queueEntry` property, which Lombok's `@Getter` exposes as `getQueueEntry()`), consumed by `undoTransition` in `QueueEntryTransitionRestController`. The front end sends it from `undoTransition` in `queue-entry-actions.resource.ts`, called by the undo-transition modal.

**Backend (openmrs-module-queue)**
- `openmrs-module-queue/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/queue/web/dto/UndoQueueEntryTransitionRequest.java` lines 14-18: the DTO declares `private String queueEntry;`. This is the field to rename.
- `openmrs-module-queue/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/queue/web/QueueEntryTransitionRestController.java` lines 99-110: the `DELETE /queue-entry/transition` handler reads `body.getQueueEntry()` at line 103 to look up the entry.

**Front end (openmrs-esm-patient-management)**
- `openmrs-esm-patient-management/packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/modals/queue-entry-actions.resource.ts` lines 63-76: the `UndoTransitionParams` interface declares `queueEntry: string`, and `undoTransition` sends `params` as the DELETE body to `queue-entry/transition`.
- `openmrs-esm-patient-management/packages/esm-service-queues-app/src/modals/undo-transition-queue-entry.modal.tsx` lines 52-55: the modal's `submitAction` builds the body as `{ queueEntry: queueEntry.uuid }`.

Renaming the field means changing the Java property (and its getter call at line 103), the TypeScript interface, and the modal's object literal together. The Java getter is generated by Lombok, so the rename follows the field name. I did not check for other clients or the openmrs-esm-patient-chart checkout, which only had one unrelated match.
